strings.widgetSettingsCompassWindStyleHelp:
Choose how wind direction is displayed on the compass.

None – wind indicator is hidden.

Arrow – classic two-tone triangular arrow pointing into the wind.

Arc – filled arc segment showing the upwind sector with a center line.

Windsock – a tapered cone resembling a real airport windsock. The wide end faces into the wind, the narrow tip blows downwind. Wind speed is encoded by the number of colored stripes (1 to 5):
1 stripe: 0–1.5 m/s (0–3 kt)
2 stripes: 1.5–3.5 m/s (3–7 kt)
3 stripes: 3.5–6 m/s (7–12 kt)
4 stripes: 6–8.5 m/s (12–17 kt)
5 stripes: 8.5+ m/s (17+ kt)

strings.widgetSettingsNextTurnpointGlideHelp:
Actual: Your actual gliding ratio.
 Computed: Glider ratio inferred from preferences adjusted for wind.
strings.widgetSettingsNextTurnpointHeightShownVa: Value is computed on actual point (for example on the cylinder, if you pick Cylinder or Optimized point above).
strings.widgetSettingsNextTurnpointSpeedTypeHelp:
Groundspeed: your actual speed over ground is used - if you flight toward the point, you will see how much time it takes (the wind is included implicitly) - but if you're circling, the value will change all the time (because of different ground speed upwind/downwind).
 Airspeed: from ground speed and wind airspeed is estimated - this should be the value indicated by pitot tube if we have any. It depends on your braking/accelerating. This value indicate when you reach the point in actual break/acc settings, IF you fly directly (but you don't need to do it - this is the difference between ground speed and airspeed).
 Glidespeed: The speed from glider configuration corrected by wind - doesn't matter how fast you're flying right now nor direction. Indicates when you reach the point if you fly directly and on configured airspeed (for example full accelerated flight speed).
 XC speed: This speed is calculated from the biggest xcdistance (distance over 3 breaking point) and flying time. Can be used for large FAI triangle hunting.

strings.widgetSettingsWebViewUrlHelp2: You can use placeholders ${lat} and ${lng} for current latitude and longitude, ${hdg} for heading in degrees, ${alt} for current GPS-altitude in meters, ${spd}: current groundspeed in m/s.
